investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach any subsequent lifecycle step.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the cluster scheduling layer rather than in the eval runner or API logic. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable slots for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating all current consumers are at equal or higher priority.

[Possible] The 4 remaining nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., missing label, wrong zone, or taint) that permanently excludes them from hosting remote-agent pods, reducing effective scheduling capacity to only 2 nodes and making the cluster more susceptible to exhaustion.
[Possible] A recent scale-up of remote-agent demand (e.g., more concurrent eval runs, increased user load on the swarm) consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval run began.

[Less likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertiser (device plugin or node feature discovery component) on one or both eligible nodes crashed or stopped reporting, causing the scheduler to see 0 available units even if physical capacity exists.
[Low likelihood] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange was tightened, reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm units schedulable per namespace.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach any subsequent lifecycle step.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the cluster scheduling layer rather than in the eval runner or API logic. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 (createAgent call) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so every pod remained unscheduled until the eval timed out, producing empty evidence and a full contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never returned a running agent, so the eval produced no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing) and the runtime check assertion "hello from aura" could never be evaluated. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. All three sibling checks share this exact message, confirming the resource is exhausted cluster-wide for this workload class.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector rules on the remote agent pod spec restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes (4 of 6 are excluded), reducing the effective scheduling domain to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, which are already saturated.

Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new eval pods from being scheduled. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is designed to release resources, but if a prior run leaked a pod, capacity would remain consumed.

Lower confidence: The eval runner itself may have been invoked multiple times in parallel (e.g., by the scheduled observability workflow), causing multiple pods to compete for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. consumed capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. If capacity is at zero, identify which pods are holding the slots and whether any are leaked eval pods.

Check for leaked remote agent pods in the eval namespace that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs. If found, manually terminate them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and re-run the eval to confirm recovery.

If kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, assess whether additional nodes with this resource need to be provisioned to support concurrent eval runs alongside production agent workloads.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 185), but the two failing siblings (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are required=true. Prioritize restoring scheduling capacity for the required checks first.

Do not treat this as a user-facing production outage based on the supplied evidence alone — no user-traffic or incident signals are present. Treat this as an eval infrastructure failure until cluster inspection confirms the scope of impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, the scheduling-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and the cause would shift to a misconfigured node affinity/selector or a pod spec error.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's specific pod spec rather than a cluster-wide resource exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained resource exhaustion.
If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes showed capacity available but the pod was still unschedulable, the node affinity/selector mismatch would become the primary cause rather than resource exhaustion.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exists on any node in the cluster, the cause would be a missing node label or resource registration rather than exhaustion.
